────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
PROGRAMME CONTEXT
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

The aiucredit ASP application is a legacy Underwriting Credit Risk platform being
modernised to a cloud-native microservices architecture. Features must be named from
the business capability perspective — they describe what the system will do for a
user, not how it is implemented.

Natural Feature boundaries for UW Credit Risk:

| EPIC domain | Typical Feature areas |
|-------------|----------------------|
| Application Intake and Eligibility | Applicant Data Capture, Eligibility Rules Enforcement, Document Upload and Verification |
| Credit Scoring and Risk Assessment | Bureau Data Retrieval, Score Calculation and Banding, Score Override and Referral Logic |
| Underwriting Decision and Workflow | Auto-Approve/Decline Rules, Referral Routing, Decision Recording and Audit |
| Approval Authority and Governance | Authority Matrix Enforcement, Escalation Workflow, Override Approval |
| Policy Issuance and Premium Calculation | Premium Calculation Engine, Quote Generation, Policy Binding and Issuance |
| Integrations and External Feeds | Credit Bureau Integration, Rating Engine Integration, Document Management, Notifications |
| Audit, Compliance, and Reporting | Immutable Decision Log, Regulatory Report Generation, MI Dashboard |
| Data Migration and Reference Data | Schema Migration, Reference Data Load, Configuration Migration |

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ANTI-HALLUCINATION RULES (enforced, no exceptions)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

1. Every SR-ID cited in a Feature's SRD traceability table MUST exist in the SRD for
   your EPIC. Never fabricate SR references.
2. Feature names, Benefit Hypothesis text, and AC criteria MUST use business terms
   from epic.md, srd.md, or the KB — never technical identifiers (class names, API
   paths, table names, service names).
4. Every Feature traces to at least one SR. A Feature with no SR citation is invalid
   and must not be included.
5. Do not generate Features for SRs belonging to another EPIC. Your scope is EPIC-{N}
   only — read your EPIC's SR list from epic.md and constrain your output to those SRs.
6. If an SR is too thin to write a specific Gherkin AC, leave the AC row blank and
   log the gap in Open Items — do NOT write bracket placeholders like "[outcome]" or
   "[precondition]". A blank row triggers the gap detector; a bracket stub silently
   propagates to user stories and generated test cases.
7. If the epic artefact is absent or unreadable, stop immediately and state exactly which input is missing. Do not continue with partial output.

GROUNDING RULES
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

1. Every Feature traces to SR-NNN. Each Feature block lists the SR identifiers it

2. Every SR in your EPIC's SR table lands in at least one Feature. After writing,

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FIELD-BY-FIELD QUALITY BAR (enforced before writing each Feature)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

FEATURE NAME:
  • Use business vocabulary — describe what users gain, not how it is implemented
  • Pattern: {Business Capability} + for/to + {Stakeholder or Outcome}
  • Never use class names, endpoint paths, table names, or SR/FR identifiers
  • Minimum 4 words
  BAD:  "BureauAdapter.fetchScore() integration"
  BAD:  "Implement SR-SCORING-001"
  BAD:  "Data processing"
  GOOD: "Credit Bureau Data Retrieval for Underwriting Assessment"
  GOOD: "Automated Premium Calculation via Rating Engine"

PRIORITY:
  • Must — SR is mandatory; blocking regulatory obligation or core business function
  • Should — SR is important but can be deferred one sprint without blocking others
  • Could — SR is desirable; no blocking impact if deferred
  • Derive from the SR priority field in the SRD. Never assign a higher priority
    than the SR carries.

STATUS:
  • Ready — all covering SRs are unblocked and the Feature can enter sprint planning
  • Blocked — at least one covering SR is marked Blocked in the SRD; state the
    reason verbatim from the SRD block note

STAKEHOLDER OWNER:
  • MUST be one of: Underwriter / Credit Risk Manager / Finance Analyst /
    Compliance Officer / IT Administrator / System / Applicant
  • Use the role most directly benefiting from the Feature — not the implementing team
  BAD:  "Dev Team"   "Platform"   "Backend"
  GOOD: "Underwriter"   "Compliance Officer"

BENEFIT HYPOTHESIS:
  • MUST follow the exact pattern:
    "We believe that {feature capability} will {business outcome} for {persona}.
     We will know this is true when {measurable criterion observable at sprint demo}."
  • The criterion MUST be demonstrable at a sprint demo — not a long-term KPI
  • Name the persona using a role from the domain table
  BAD:  "We believe this feature will improve the system for users."
  BAD:  "We believe that bureau integration will work correctly."
  GOOD: "We believe that automated credit bureau data retrieval will eliminate the
         45-minute manual bureau check cycle for Underwriters. We will know this is
         true when 95% of bureau checks complete and populate credit_score and
         risk_band without manual intervention at sprint demo."

GHERKIN ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
  • Format: "Given {specific precondition}, when {specific action or event}, then
    {verifiable outcome — field names, measurable result, or error message}."
  • MUST include at least one failure / error path per Feature (unavailability,
    timeout, invalid data, constraint violation)
  • Never write "the feature works correctly" or "the result is shown"
  • If an SR is too thin to write a specific Then clause, leave the AC row BLANK and
    log the gap in Open Items — do NOT write bracket placeholders
  • 2–5 criteria per Feature; fewer than 2 is insufficient for QA planning
  BAD:  "Given the system is running, when the feature is used, then it succeeds."
  GOOD: "Given an application has a valid nino and bureau_status = PENDING, when the
         system triggers the bureau check at submission, then credit_score and
         risk_band are stored within 30 seconds; if BureauService is unavailable, the
         application status is set to BUREAU_PENDING and the Underwriter receives an
         alert."

#### Benefit Hypothesis
We believe that automated credit bureau data retrieval will eliminate the current
45-minute manual bureau check cycle for Underwriters. We will know this is true when

| ID        | Criterion |
|-----------|-----------|

| AC-1-01-3 | Given a bureau response returns a credit_score below the minimum threshold defined in SR-SCORING-002, then the system automatically flags the application for DECLINE review and notifies the Underwriter. |

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FEATURE TYPES AND WHEN TO USE THEM
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

STANDARD feature:
  Default type. A user-facing capability derived from one or more SRs. Use for any
  Feature that is not compliance-driven, integration-specific, or blocked.

COMPLIANCE / AUDIT feature:
  Use when the covering SR references a regulation, audit obligation, record retention,
  or data privacy requirement.
  — Stakeholder owner: always "Compliance Officer" unless the SR names a different role
  — Benefit Hypothesis: must reference the specific regulation name or inspection SLA
  — AC must include: (a) audit fields stored, (b) immutability or retention rule,
    (c) retrieval SLA, (d) failure / rollback behaviour
  — Priority: always Must for regulatory requirements

INTEGRATION feature:
  Use when the SR covers an external system integration (bureau, rating engine,
  document management, notification service).
  — Feature name must identify the external system by name
  — Benefit Hypothesis must name the external system and the data or event exchanged
  — AC must include: (a) happy path with field names and SLAs, (b) unavailability /
    timeout path, (c) retry or fallback behaviour

BLOCKED feature:
  Use when any covering SR is marked Blocked in the SRD.
  — Write the Identity block fully; set Status to "Blocked — {reason from SRD}"
  — Add a BLOCKED banner immediately after the H3 title
  — Write Benefit Hypothesis and ACs as "[Blocked — {reason}]"
  — Log in the Open Items Blocked Features table

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
SAFe FEATURE DEFINITION
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

- A Feature is a service or function that fulfils a stakeholder need and is sized for
  one sprint (plan, build, test, and demo in 2 weeks).
- Features are named from the user perspective, not the implementation perspective.
- Each Feature has one Benefit Hypothesis following the exact pattern above.
- Each Feature has 2–5 Gherkin acceptance criteria — the definition of done at demo.
- Target 3–8 Features per EPIC. Fewer than 2 Features means the Feature is too coarse
  for a sprint; more than 10 means the EPIC should have been split.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
SR COVERAGE VERIFICATION (run after writing all Features)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

After writing all Features for your EPIC:
1. List every SR-ID assigned to your EPIC in epic.md.
2. For each SR-ID, verify it appears in at least one Feature's SRD traceability table.
3. Any SR-ID with no Feature coverage → add to Open Items as "Uncovered SR".
4. Any SR-ID covered by more than one Feature → add Open Item noting the overlap and
   recommend whether to consolidate or keep split.
